[F8 F4 F2] [NS-0 NS-1 NS-3 NS-8]

claims.assertion: The driver cancelled the trip for a reason of his own, not because the rider failed to show: at 08:52 he wrote 'Sorry ah, my kid's school called, I have to go now. Cancelling.' (F11), and his own written statement repeats it — 'my kid's school called and I had to go, so I had to cancel' (F14). That is a personal/family matter, not rider no-show, so the cancellation falls under NS-3 and no fee may be charged.

The app reason 'rider_no_show' (F4) does not decide the case: NS-0 turns on why the driver actually cancelled, and his contemporaneous chat message (F11) and post-trip statement (F14) both give a family reason. A no-show fee cannot stand on a reason the driver himself contradicts.

In any event the $5.00 must be refunded in full: the record shows a charged cancellation fee of $5.00 (F8, F4) with no basis under NS-1 because the driver abandoned the waiting himself at 08:52:10 (F4, F11). NS-3 provides that where the driver cancelled for another reason, no fee applies and any fee charged is refunded in full.

The driver's arrival conditions do not save the fee: he tapped 'I'm Here' at 08:46:10, 40 m from the pickup (F7), and stayed within 200 m for 6 min 0 s after the tap (F7, F2), but NS-1 requires the no-show to be the reason for cancelling — his messages show it was not (F11, F14). Nothing about his car trouble, waiting or presence can convert a family errand into a rider no-show.

No traffic or weather condition could justify the cancellation as anything else: there were no speed-band records and no incidents near the route during the trip window (F15, F16) and the weather was fair (F17), so the only documented cause of the cancellation is the driver's own personal matter (F11, F14).

The rider's complaint ('By the time I came out he had cancelled, and I was charged $5.00 anyway') is consistent with the timeline: the driver cancelled 8 min 10 s after acceptance (F4) after only 6 min 15 s cumulative presence near the pickup (F2), and the rider has no prior no-show history (F18: 0 no-show disputes, 0 upheld in 90 days), which weighs against a no-show finding.

The driver already has 1 upheld no-show-related dispute in the last 90 days (F19), so if the court finds the cancellation improper, RD-6-style repeat treatment supports an account flag on the driver as an add-on to the refund.

The rider never answered the 08:47 in-app call (F13) and sent no chat reply (F10, F12), so the driver will argue the rider was simply not coming out.

claims.assertion: The driver arrived at the pickup point: he tapped "I'm Here" at 08:46:10 while 40 m from the pickup point and GPS puts his closest approach at 38 m, well inside the 200 m radius required by NS-1(i).

The free-wait threshold was satisfied: he was within 200 m of the pickup from 08:45:55 and had accumulated 6 min 15 s inside the radius before cancelling at 08:52:10, exceeding the 5-minute free wait counted from the later of scheduled pickup and arrival (arrival recorded 08:46:10).

He stayed at the pickup point throughout the wait: GPS shows him stationary at (1.3250, 103.9299), 40 m from the pickup, for the whole period 08:46:10–08:52:10, with no gap that leaves presence unproven.

He made exactly the contact NS-1(iii) requires before cancelling: two in-app messages (the first at 08:46:40: "Reached, white BYD e6, waiting at the pickup.") and one in-app call at 08:47:40, all before the 08:52:10 cancellation, and the chat record is complete and timestamped.

The rider never appeared during the six minutes the driver waited: the record shows no rider response to the message at 08:46:40 or the call at 08:47:40, and the cancellation was entered in the app under the reason rider_no_show, so the $5.00 fee under NS-1 stands and was not refundable to the rider.

The record contains no traffic, weather or route cause for the delay: no speed-band or incident records for the trip window, fair weather, and no off-route segment, so the wait arose solely from the rider's non-appearance at the pickup point.

The driver's rating is 4.87 across 1,290 trips in 90 days and his single prior no-show dispute arose from him legitimately waiting and cancelling rather than any chargeable abuse; the rider's profile is not relevant to the NS-1 conditions, which are all independently met by the GPS and timeline records.
